TIAGO FERRÃO-LINDQVIST
Data Engineering | Test & Validation Engineering
[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LOCATION]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Test & Validation Engineer with experience building Python tools to process and report on engineering test data, working with SQL Server staging data, and developing Power BI dashboards for validation and design teams. Processes data from six test rigs and supports colleagues through reusable internal tooling. Currently completing an online data engineering course, with six of nine modules finished. Brings a mechanical engineering background in durability and vibration testing, root-cause analysis, pump design and FEA.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Programming and data processing: Python, pandas, NumPy, SQL, MATLAB, Simulink
Data and reporting: SQL Server, SQLite, Power BI, Matplotlib, npTDMS
Tools: Flask, Docker Compose, Git, Windows Task Scheduler
Engineering: Durability and vibration testing, test-data processing, root-cause analysis, structural FEA

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Test & Validation Engineer | Corvane Automotive Components | 2019–Present
- Conduct durability and vibration testing, support root-cause analysis, and develop tools for processing and reporting test data.
- Built Python scripts to parse TDMS and CSV output from six rigs (about 2 GB per week), flag channels outside test specifications, and generate report figures.
- Set up the scripts to run nightly on a lab PC using Windows Task Scheduler and write summary results to a staging table in the plant’s SQL Server database.
- Packaged the tool for internal use; four other test engineers now use it for their own tests.
- Created a Power BI dashboard using the staging data to show pass/fail trends and cycles to failure by product generation; used by about 15 engineers in validation and design.
- Trained three apprentices in rig safety and test setup (2022–2024).
- Used TIA Portal, with an automation engineer supervising, to adjust PLC setpoints and timers.

Mechanical Design Engineer | Halvik Pumps | 2014–2019
- Designed pump casings and impellers and carried out structural FEA.
- Supported the performance test bench and wrote a LabVIEW data-acquisition program that reduced test setup time from about two hours to 30 minutes.

SELECTED PROJECTS
Rig Data Processing and Reporting Tool | Corvane Automotive Components | 2021–Present
Python scripts process rig output (TDMS and CSV), flag channels outside test specifications, generate report figures, and write summary results to a SQL Server staging table. Runs nightly on a lab PC and is used by four other test engineers.
Technologies: Python, pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, npTDMS, SQL Server, Windows Task Scheduler

Test Results Dashboard | Corvane Automotive Components | 2023
Built a Power BI dashboard showing pass/fail trends and cycles to failure per product generation, used by about 15 validation and design engineers.
Technologies: Power BI, SQL

Adjuster Drive Load-Profile Model | Corvane Automotive Components | 2020–Present
Developed a MATLAB/Simulink model of a seat-adjuster drive, including motor, gearbox and rail friction, to select rig load profiles matching customer duty cycles.
Technologies: MATLAB, Simulink

Bike-Sharing Trips API | Personal Learning Project | 2025
Built a small Flask API over a public bike-sharing dataset loaded into SQLite, with three read-only endpoints. Runs locally; followed a tutorial to run it with Docker Compose.
Technologies: Python, Flask, SQLite, Docker Compose, Git

PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
Online Data Engineering Course | In progress
Completed 6 of 9 modules; no certificate awarded.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, well structured, quantified, and professionally written. It presents a credible progression from mechanical engineering and testing into engineering data tooling. Strong evidence includes processing approximately 2 GB of data per week from six rigs, adoption by four engineers, dashboard usage by approximately 15 engineers, and the reduction of test setup time from two hours to 30 minutes. The content is appropriately cautious about the candidate's experience and does not overstate cloud, platform, or senior data-engineering expertise. The main content weaknesses are the repeated descriptions of the same projects in both Professional Experience and Selected Projects, the absence of a Languages section, and the use of contact placeholders rather than usable contact details.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses conventional headings, readable text, standard chronology, and keyword-rich skills that should parse well in most ATS systems. Relevant terms such as Python, SQL, SQL Server, Power BI, Docker Compose, Git, data processing, test data, and reusable tooling are present. However, the profile is unlikely to pass a strict Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform screen because it does not demonstrate the ad's core platform terms: Google Cloud, BigQuery, Cloud Run, GKE, Airflow, dbt, CI/CD, query optimisation, dimensional modelling, data governance, or access policies. These are genuine experience gaps, not keywords that should be added without evidence. The [EMAIL], [PHONE], and [LOCATION] placeholders are also a serious practical and parsing issue if they appear in the submitted version. Estimated AI/ATS screening probability for this specific senior role is low to moderate, mainly because of the seniority, cloud, platform-scale, modelling, and production-operation requirements rather than because of formatting.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: This is a truthful and comparatively strong CV for test-data engineering, engineering analytics, or junior-to-mid-level data engineering work. It aligns with the role's emphasis on reusable frameworks, internal tooling, data processing, BI collaboration, and support for colleagues: the tool is reused by four engineers, the dashboard serves validation and design teams, and the candidate trained three apprentices. The personal Flask project and ongoing data-engineering course provide evidence of learning and experimentation with open-source technologies, although they do not establish production platform experience. The CV does not show experience designing or operating a production data platform or cloud warehouse at scale; advanced Python and SQL with query optimisation on large datasets; strong data modelling; Google Cloud or a comparable cloud; graph modelling; or the listed platform stack. Portuguese is supported by the candidate information but is not currently stated in the CV. The document itself demonstrates good professional written English. Overall, the candidate is substantially below the advertised Senior Data Engineer level but presents a credible adjacent profile if Halden Pay genuinely considers junior or mid-level applicants.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. CRITICAL — In the contact header, replace `[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LOCATION]` with the candidate's actual professional email address, phone number, and location before submitting the CV. Keep the information in one simple text line so ATS parsers can identify it reliably.

2. In the Professional Development section, add the course name if it is available in the candidate's materials, and retain the truthful progress statement: `Completed 6 of 9 modules; no certificate awarded.` Do not imply that the course is a certification or that the remaining modules are completed.

3. Add a `LANGUAGES` section after Technical Skills or Professional Development and include `Portuguese` because the candidate information identifies him as Portuguese. Add an English proficiency label only if the candidate can substantiate a specific level; otherwise, the CV's professional English is already evident from the document itself.

4. In the Professional Summary, make the level and scope of the data experience more precise by changing `Test & Validation Engineer with experience building Python tools to process and report on engineering test data` to `Test & Validation Engineer with experience building internal Python tooling for engineering test-data processing and reporting`. This keeps the strong match to reusable tooling while avoiding an implication of production data-platform ownership.

5. In the Corvane Automotive Components experience section, clarify the database scope in the SQL Server bullet by changing `write summary results to a staging table in the plant’s SQL Server database` to `write summary results to an IT-created staging table in the plant’s SQL Server database`. This accurately reflects the candidate's stated permissions and avoids suggesting database-schema ownership.

6. Reduce duplication between Professional Experience and Selected Projects only if space is needed. Keep the quantified outcomes in Professional Experience, and shorten the corresponding project entries to focus on architecture and technologies—for example, retain the project title, one concise description, and the Technologies line. Do not remove the six rigs, 2 GB per week, four users, or 15 engineers entirely; these are the CV's strongest evidence of impact.
critique.critical_issues: The contact details are still placeholders (`[EMAIL]`, `[PHONE]`, `[LOCATION]`). This must be corrected before submission. No unsupported skills, tools, certifications, cloud experience, or production-platform claims were detected when the CV was cross-referenced against the candidate information.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, truthful, well structured, and professionally written. It presents a credible transition from mechanical/test engineering into data engineering and includes useful evidence such as six test rigs, approximately 2 GB of weekly data, four internal users, and approximately 15 dashboard users. The project section reinforces the strongest technical evidence. The main content weaknesses are incomplete contact details, omission of English despite the English-language original application, and some duplication between Professional Experience and Selected Projects. The document also does not clearly distinguish production-like internal automation from formal data-platform engineering, although this is primarily a job-alignment limitation rather than a writing defect.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The simple section headings, reverse-chronological experience, standard bullet format, and text-based presentation should parse well in most ATS systems. Relevant keywords supported by the candidate's material include Python, pandas, NumPy, SQL Server, Power BI, Docker Compose, Git, Flask, SQLite, MATLAB, Simulink, data processing, reporting, test data, and Windows Task Scheduler. AI screening probability for this specific Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform role is low to moderate because the CV does not contain supported evidence for cloud platforms, BigQuery, Airflow, dbt, CI/CD, advanced SQL/query optimisation, data modelling, or production data platforms at scale. These are genuine experience gaps rather than keywords that should be added. The [EMAIL], [PHONE], and [LOCATION] placeholders also make the document incomplete for an actual application.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV shows relevant foundations for reusable internal tooling, data processing, reporting, collaboration with validation and design teams, and practical ownership of a recurring automated process. Training apprentices and packaging a tool used by four engineers support the company's Together and Ownership themes; the reduction of test setup time from about two hours to 30 minutes supports a practical Pace-oriented impact. However, the candidate's material explicitly states there is no cloud experience, no formal data-platform or cloud-warehouse ownership, no schema design, no query optimisation on large datasets, no dimensional or graph modelling, and no Airflow, dbt, Spark, Kafka, or CI/CD experience. The profile is therefore substantially below the advertised senior data-platform requirement, though it may be credible for a junior or mid-level data-engineering pathway. Portuguese is shown. English is evidenced by the original English cover letter but is not shown in the CV.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL:
1. In the contact line beneath the candidate's name, replace [EMAIL] and [PHONE] with the candidate's actual contact details. Replace [LOCATION] with "Porto, Portugal", which is supported by the original candidate information. Do not leave bracketed placeholders in the submitted CV.
2. In the LANGUAGES section, add English with an accurate proficiency level supported by the candidate's demonstrated English-language application materials; for example, "English — professional working proficiency" only if that accurately reflects the candidate's broader ability. Retain "Portuguese". This makes the English requirement visible without adding unsupported technical claims.
3. In the Professional Summary, make the seniority and scope of the current data work precise rather than allowing it to read like a formal enterprise data platform. Replace "Test & Validation Engineer with experience building internal Python tooling for engineering test-data processing and reporting" with wording such as "Test & Validation Engineer building reusable internal Python tooling for engineering test-data processing, validation checks, and reporting." This preserves the strongest match while avoiding overstatement.

MINOR:
4. In Professional Experience under Corvane Automotive Components, keep the quantified bullets as the primary evidence and remove or consolidate the repeated descriptions in Selected Projects where the same project is described almost verbatim. For example, retain the detailed project under Selected Projects and shorten the corresponding experience bullet to its operational outcome, or retain the experience bullets and reduce each project entry to one-line scope plus technologies. This will improve scanability without removing evidence.
5. In the Corvane experience section, make the operational nature of the automation explicit by changing "Set up the scripts to run nightly on a lab PC" to "Automated nightly execution on a lab PC using Windows Task Scheduler, processing approximately 2 GB of weekly TDMS and CSV output and writing summary results to an IT-created SQL Server staging table." This uses supported facts and better surfaces operating/automation experience for ATS and human reviewers.
6. In the Bike-Sharing Trips API project, retain the limitation that it runs locally and was tutorial-guided, but make the learning purpose clearer by changing the opening to "Built a personal learning Flask API over a public bike-sharing dataset loaded into SQLite; implemented three read-only endpoints and used Git and Docker Compose for local execution." This presents the project positively without implying production deployment or independent Docker expertise.
critique.critical_issues:
1. The submitted CV contains incomplete contact placeholders: [EMAIL], [PHONE], and [LOCATION]. These must be replaced before submission.
2. English is not listed in the CV even though the original candidate material includes a substantial English-language cover letter. This is a material omission for a role explicitly requiring good professional English.
3. No unsupported skills or experience were detected. The CV does not falsely claim cloud, BigQuery, Airflow, dbt, CI/CD, advanced SQL optimisation, or data-platform ownership, which is appropriate and should be preserved.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a clear, truthful, well-structured CV with strong quantified evidence: six rigs, approximately 2 GB per week, four internal users, 15 dashboard users, and measurable test-setup savings. The progression from mechanical design to test and validation engineering is credible, and the project section makes the candidate's data-related work easy to identify. The content is professional and appropriately cautious about the scope of the candidate's Python, SQL Server, Docker Compose, and PLC experience. The main content weakness is some repetition between the Corvane experience bullets and the Selected Projects section, which slightly reduces concision.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard section headings, plain text formatting, conventional reverse-chronological experience, and ATS-readable technology lists. It includes relevant supported keywords such as Python, pandas, NumPy, SQL Server, Power BI, Docker Compose, Git, Flask, SQLite, MATLAB, and Simulink. However, AI/ATS screening for this specific Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform role is likely to be low-to-moderate because the CV does not contain supported evidence for core screening terms including cloud platforms, BigQuery, Airflow, dbt, data modelling, cloud data warehouses, query optimisation, CI/CD, or production data platforms at scale. Those are candidate-experience gaps rather than wording defects, so they should not be inserted without evidence. The Skills section could also distinguish workplace technologies from personal-project technologies more explicitly.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with the reusable-framework aspect of the role: the candidate built an internal tool used by four other engineers, automated nightly processing, created reporting for validation and design stakeholders, and supported colleagues through training. These examples provide credible evidence of ownership, collaboration, practical data quality checks, and interest in data engineering. The candidate is nevertheless a substantial technical match gap for this senior platform role. The candidate's own material states that they have no cloud experience, have not used Airflow, dbt, Spark, or Kafka, have not designed a database schema, have not performed query optimisation on large datasets, and have not operated a production data platform or cloud warehouse at scale. The CV also does not establish professional English proficiency as a stated language qualification, although it is written in English. Portuguese is correctly shown as a plus. The document should present the existing engineering-data experience accurately rather than attempting to position it as equivalent to senior cloud data-platform experience.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Technical Skills section, change the Tools line to make project-only exposure explicit: "Tools: Flask; Docker Compose (personal learning project); Git (personal repositories since 2025); Windows Task Scheduler." This prevents recruiters from assuming Docker Compose and Git were used in the Corvane production environment.
2. In the Selected Projects section, reduce repetition with the Professional Experience section. Keep the detailed technical description in the project entries, but shorten the corresponding Corvane experience bullets to focus on responsibilities and outcomes—for example, retain the figures about six rigs, four users, and 15 dashboard users in one location rather than repeating the same full project description twice.
3. In the Professional Summary section, make the distinction between engineering test-data automation and data-platform engineering explicit while preserving the current truthful positioning. For example, change the opening to: "Test & Validation Engineer with hands-on experience building internal Python tooling for engineering test-data processing and reporting, automating scheduled workflows on a lab PC, working with SQL Server staging data, and developing Power BI dashboards." This improves role relevance without implying cloud or production-platform experience.
4. In the Rig Data Processing and Reporting Tool project entry, retain the existing statement that the SQL Server table was IT-created or revise the wording to "writes summary results to an IT-managed SQL Server staging table." This accurately communicates the candidate's contribution and avoids suggesting database-schema ownership.
